issues.title: Missing Join with Merchant Table
issues.problem: The query does not join the dim_merchant table, but the business rule requires merchant names to be shown.
issues.fix: LEFT JOIN sigma_analytics.dim_merchant m ON c.merchant_id = m.merchant_id

issues.title: Incorrect Aggregation for Lifetime Value
issues.problem: The query calculates lifetime value for all transactions, not just completed ones, which violates the business rule.
issues.fix: SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) as lifetime_value

issues.title: Incorrect Grouping for Total Orders
issues.problem: The query groups by customer_name, email, which might lead to incorrect total orders if customers have the same name and email.
issues.fix: GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name, c.email, c.tier

issues.title: Lack of Comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic, which makes it harder to understand.
issues.fix: Add comments explaining the purpose of each clause.

review.corrected_sql:
SELECT c.customer_name, c.email, c.tier,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) as lifetime_value,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.transaction_id ELSE NULL END) as total_orders
FROM dim_customer c
LEFT JOIN fact_transactions t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id
LEFT JOIN sigma_analytics.dim_merchant m ON c.merchant_id = m.merchant_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name, c.email, c.tier
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) > 1000
ORDER BY lifetime_value DESC;
review.summary: The query had issues with missing joins, incorrect aggregations, and readability. Fixes included joining the merchant table, correctly calculating lifetime value, and improving grouping and readability.

issues.title: Incorrect calculation of failure rate
issues.problem: The failure rate is being calculated incorrectly because the failed_count is being calculated per row, not per group.
issues.fix: Use a subquery to calculate the failed_count and total_count separately.

issues.title: Correlated subquery
issues.line: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_transactions f2 WHERE f2.status = 'FAILED' AND f2.transaction_date = t.transaction_date
issues.problem: The correlated subquery can be inefficient as it runs for each row in the outer query.
issues.fix: Use a JOIN to calculate the failed_count.

issues.title: Lack of comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic, which makes it harder to understand.
issues.fix: Add comments to explain the logic of the query.

review.corrected_sql:
WITH transaction_counts AS (
  SELECT
    transaction_date,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'FAILED' THEN 1 END) as failed_count,
    COUNT(*) as total_count
  FROM fact_transactions
  GROUP BY transaction_date
)
SELECT
  t.transaction_date,
  tc.failed_count,
  tc.total_count,
  (tc.failed_count * 1.0 / tc.total_count) * 100 as failure_rate
FROM transaction_counts tc
ORDER BY t.transaction_date;
review.summary: The query had issues with the calculation of the failure rate, a correlated subquery affecting performance, and a lack of comments for readability.

issues.title: Incorrect Revenue Calculation
issues.problem: The query sums all transaction amounts without filtering for 'COMPLETED' status.
issues.fix: SUM(CASE WHEN b.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN b.amount ELSE 0 END) AS s

issues.title: Correlated Subquery
issues.problem: The correlated subquery can be inefficient as it runs for each row in the result set.

issues.title: Implicit Join Syntax
issues.line: FROM dim_customer a, fact_transactions b, dim_merchant c
issues.problem: Implicit join syntax is less readable and more prone to errors.
issues.fix: Use explicit JOIN syntax for better readability.

issues.title: Lack of Comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic, especially around the revenue calculation and failure rate.
issues.fix: Add comments explaining the logic of the query.

review.corrected_sql:
WITH failed_transactions AS (
  SELECT x.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS failed_count
  FROM fact_transactions x
  WHERE x.status = 'FAILED'
  GROUP BY x.customer_id
)
SELECT a.customer_name,
       a.email,
       a.tier,
       a.city,
       SUM(CASE WHEN b.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN b.amount ELSE 0 END) AS revenue,
       COALESCE(f.failed_count, 0) AS failed_count
FROM dim_customer a
JOIN fact_transactions b ON a.customer_id = b.customer_id
JOIN dim_merchant c ON b.merchant_id = c.merchant_id
LEFT JOIN failed_transactions f ON a.customer_id = f.customer_id
WHERE c.category = 'Food Delivery'
GROUP BY a.customer_name, a.email, a.tier, a.city, a.customer_id
ORDER BY revenue DESC;
review.summary: The query had issues with revenue calculation, performance due to a correlated subquery, readability with implicit joins, and lacked comments.
